thread:
maya: Quick sync — ran the ownership-demarcation experiment on cohort-B last night. TL;DR: functional correctness ✅, confidence high on request routing, but 95th pct latency and GPU utilization tails spiked. tagging @sanjay for visibility :eyes:
sanjay: can you paste the perf numbers and what broke the tail?
maya: paste below — numbers are from 02:00–05:00 UTC window. small table:
```
cohort: B
requests: 420k
p50 latency: 34ms
p95 latency: 420ms
p99 latency: 1.2s
avg gpu util: 68%
peak gpu util (tail): 98% (short spikes)
cache hit rate: 12% (vs 31% baseline)
```
maya: root cause hypothesis: the demarcation adds an extra adapter hop that decreases locality for requests that would otherwise hit cached prefixes; continuous batching also desynchronized for certain seq lengths -> bigger KV bake/repop windows.
owen: did we see any error spike / SLO breaches from clients?
maya: no 5xx spike, error budget still fine, but per-route latency SLO near threshold for a few customers in cohort-B.
lucy: thanks — sounds like a regression in cache locality. Did the rollout change batching config or quantization profiles?
maya: rollout only toggled ownership routing flag and lightweight adapter. batching config unchanged, quant profiles unchanged. but routing causes more cross-pod fanout for long-context requests.
sanjay: ok that explains the cache hit drop. Two quick asks: 1) can we instrument per-pod cache hit rate split by ownership tag? 2) can we simulate reorder of requests to measure desync effect?
maya: working on (1) — added heatmap metric (ownership_tag -> pod -> cache_hit) in the test cluster already. (2) planning a replay job tomorrow against traffic sample.
owen: any low-friction mitigations we can toggle now while we dig? e.g., reduce cross-pod sharding, fall back to previous routing for heavy contexts, or increase batched window?
maya: options sketched:
- toggle back cohort-B to stable routing (fast rollback)
- enable affinity shim: prefer last-known pod for session tokens (soft affinity)
- adjust batch-agg window to prefer shorter waits for long-context requests
- cache prewarming for known hot prefixes on rollout
I think soft affinity + prewarm is lowest risk.
lucy: soft affinity makes sense; also we should update the runbook docs describing ownership tag semantics and rollback matrix. I can draft.
infra-bot: deploy job #r-2024-443 applied to cluster-staging by maya (started 2024-06-11T02:13:45Z)
sanjay: agree with soft affinity + prewarm. we should also gate full rollout on heatmap threshold: if per-pod cache hit delta > 10% for any major tenant, stop.
maya: solid. I'll add the heatmap threshold and a canary window of 1h, plus automated abort if p95 increases >20% over baseline for a tenant.
owen: do we need a quick spike budget for the dedicated pools? customers on Dedicated might get noisy neighbor problems.
maya: spoke to capacity yesterday — we can reserve a small buffer and prioritize affinity for dedicated pools; adding that to the rollout checklist.
lucy: let's schedule a short postmortem thread after the replay job: list of follow-ups, owner, ETA. I'll own the docs + checklist update.
sanjay: timeline?
maya: replay tomorrow morning, heatmap available within 2h of replay finish, I'll post results by EOD. If heatmap shows >8% cache loss for any tenant, rollback.
lucy: adding two action items: 1) docs + rollback runbook (lucy) 2) infra gating flag and affinity shim (owen + maya) 3) post-replay decisions (team)
owen: noted. I'll make the affinity shim small and feature-flagged, aim to land by 09:00 UTC.
maya: thanks. will also prepare the prewarm list for top 50 prefixes per tenant.
lucy: ping me when the replay finishes, I'll start the doc skeleton.
infra-bot: monitor alert created: ownership-demarcation.p95 > baseline*1.2 (alert id ad-3142)
maya: cool. final note — this experiment validated ownership semantics and reduced cross-tenant entanglement in happy path. worth pursuing but we need these mitigations before broader rollout.
sanjay: agreed. solid experiment, thanks maya. we'll reconvene after the replay. :thumbsup:
